description:
FILED s470bv (Opus, 2026-09-06) while shipping #1224.  PRE-EXISTING.
NOT FIXED HERE: #1224 is a `cl/` change and this is a `Pl/` change, whose bars
(generation bump + the three artifacts + tools/corpus-diff.pl +
tools/emission-ab.pl) do not belong in a runtime-only commit.

THE SHAPE.  perl's PerlIO_parse_layers accepts a layer NAME with or without a
leading colon -- `binmode FH, "utf8"` and `binmode FH, ":utf8"` are the same
thing, and so are `use open IO => "utf8"` and `use open IO => ":utf8"`
(measured against perl 5.40.3; probe scratch/s470bv/p-useopen.pl in the s470bv
worktree).  #1224 fixed every RUNTIME reader of that grammar (%p-split-layers,
%p-split-open-mode, %p-binmode-impl, %p-open-impl and p-use-open's `:std`
classifier).

The COMPILE-TIME reader was not touched, and it is a second copy of the same
rule.  Pl/Parser.pm, sub `_use_open_layers` (~line 8879):

    for my $w (@words) {
      if    ($w eq 'IN')  { $slot = 'in';   next }
      elsif ($w eq 'OUT') { $slot = 'out';  next }
      elsif ($w eq 'IO')  { $slot = 'both'; next }
      if (lc($w) eq ':std') { $std = 1; next }
      next unless $w =~ /^:/;          # <-- HERE
      ...
    }

A colon-less layer word is silently dropped, `open_regions_of` then sees
(undef, undef) and `next unless defined $in || defined $out` skips the region
entirely, so #1222's lexical `use open` carries NOTHING to the open sites in
that scope.  Silent: no announcement, no drop, the program just reads bytes.

REPRODUCER (perl vs PCL):

    use open IO => "utf8";
    open(my $fh, "<", $f) or die;      # $f holds the UTF-8 octets of "\x{100}x"
    my $s = <$fh>;
    print length($s), "\n";           # perl: 2   PCL: 3

    # and the working spelling, for contrast
    use open IO => ":utf8";           # both: 2

FIX (one line, plus its bars).  The word classifier must accept a layer name
with or without the colon -- i.e. the same grammar %p-split-layers now
implements: a word that is not IN/OUT/IO and not `:std` IS a layer, colon or
not (perl treats `:` purely as a separator).  Keep the `:std` test
case-insensitive as it is.  Normalise to the colon form before it is handed to
the emitter so the runtime sees what it sees today.

WHY IT IS GUARD-ROW TERRITORY.  The colon-less spelling of `use open` occurs in
NONE of the four populations (perl-tests, the perl companion suite, the cpan
board, Pl/t) -- measured by grep -- so corpus-diff and emission-ab will both be
IDENTICAL and the guard rows ARE the bar (the s371 rule).  Put them in
Pl/t/io-layers-01.t beside #1224's, inverse-verified on a worktree of the
commit before the fix.

BARS: gen bump (v2-850 was reserved for s470bv), the three artifacts,
tools/corpus-diff.pl, tools/emission-ab.pl over lib/**/*.pm, the gate, and --
because it is a `Pl/` emission change -- the full perl-tests sweep.
subject: `use open IO => "utf8"` (a layer name with NO leading colon) is DISCARDED at compile time: Pl::Parser::_use_open_layers keeps only words matching /^:/, so the pragma has no effect on the scope -- the runtime half of the same grammar was fixed by #1224
